statement: The exact kinetic-energy and enstrophy scalar balances, imposed on smooth solenoidal periodic paths, do not by themselves imply finite L4_t L6_x norm or time-integrable critical high-strain threshold.
hypotheses: Fixed viscosity nu>0; periodic smooth fields for t<T; scalar balances only, not assumed momentum PDE.
definitions: K=integral |u|²; E=integral |curl u|²; D=integral |grad curl u|²; S=integral omega dot (omega dot grad)u.
source_locators: NS-B001 localized seed; Tao arXiv:1402.0290 (related energy-only obstruction); Prodi-Serrin survey doi:10.1007/s00028-020-00645-3.
proof_or_gap: Choose positive stretching compact seed W, rescale amplitude to satisfy S-nu D=nu E²/K, then let lambda'=2nu E/K lambda³. The concentrated path satisfies both scalar identities exactly; critical spacetime norm and required high-strain threshold integral diverge. No momentum PDE is established.
implication_to_claim: Rules out deriving the registered critical bound using just these scalar balances and spatial solenoidality, even with finite integrated enstrophy.
unproved_dependencies: Actual PDE-dependent constraint excluding this concentrating behavior, or direct proof of integrable critical threshold for actual solutions.
adversarial_findings: Path is not established as a Navier-Stokes solution. No singularity of the actual equation claimed. Exact rational checks use arbitrary constants, not measured seed values.
